terms.meaning: Place every rectangular module (and choose its shape) inside the chip area so that nothing overlaps, everything fits the outline, and the result is compact with short wires.
terms.notConfuse: Placement usually means thousands of standard cells; floorplanning handles a few large blocks.

terms.meaning: A rectangle of fixed width w and height h, named A–E here. Its coordinate (x, y) is the lower-left corner.
terms.notConfuse: “Module 06” is the name of this course unit, not the geometric object.

terms.meaning: The allowed area W × H, here 10 × 8. Every block must lie inside [0, W] × [0, H].
terms.notConfuse: The bounding box is what the blocks actually occupy and changes with the pair; the outline is given and fixed.

terms.meaning: Two permutations (pos, neg) of the same block ids. The order of any two blocks in both decides whether they are left/right or below/above.
terms.notConfuse: A sequence pair encodes relative positions, not coordinates; coordinates come from longest paths.

terms.meaning: The two permutations. The literature also writes Γ⁺, Γ⁻ or S1, S2.
terms.notConfuse: Some textbooks mirror the vertical rule; that equals this lesson’s convention with pos and neg swapped (see § limits).

terms.meaning: One of four for every pair: left, right, below, above. Here: before in both → left; before in pos, after in neg → below.
terms.notConfuse: “Left of” does not mean touching; it only requires x[j] ≥ x[i] + w[i].

terms.meaning: An edge i → j for every “i left of j”, meaning x[j] ≥ x[i] + w[i].
terms.notConfuse: No incoming H edge does not mean leftmost; it means nothing must be to its left, so x = 0.

terms.meaning: An edge i → j for every “i below j”, meaning y[j] ≥ y[i] + h[i].
terms.notConfuse: Each pair goes into exactly one of H and V, never both.

terms.meaning: A directed graph with no cycle. H and V are DAGs because every edge points forward in pos.
terms.notConfuse: Acyclicity is guaranteed by the permutations; no separate check is needed.

terms.meaning: The largest total weight of a path into a node of a weighted DAG. Here the weight is the predecessor’s width (or height), and the result is the smallest feasible coordinate.
terms.notConfuse: Taking the maximum is not about spreading blocks out: every incoming edge is a lower bound and all must hold.

terms.meaning: An order of the nodes in which every edge points forward. pos itself is a topological order of both H and V.
terms.notConfuse: A topological order is not unique; following pos keeps the trace predictable.

terms.meaning: All coordinates computed from a pair. Each block slides as far left and down as its constraints allow.
terms.notConfuse: Different pairs can give the same packing: 3 pairs share the instructor’s packing.

terms.meaning: The smallest rectangle from the origin to (max(x+w), max(y+h)). The instructor’s pair gives 9 × 4.
terms.notConfuse: A small box does not mean it fits: 12 × 3 has area 36 too, but is wider than 10.

terms.meaning: Two blocks whose intersection has positive area. Sharing an edge or a corner (touching) is not overlap.
terms.notConfuse: A packing from a sequence pair never overlaps; fit is what must be checked separately.

terms.meaning: Bounding-box width ≤ W and height ≤ H. 13,680 of the 14,400 five-block pairs fit.
terms.notConfuse: Non-overlap and fit are two questions; a valid pair can still overflow.

terms.meaning: Total block area ÷ outline area (23 / 80 = 28.75 %), and 80 − 23 = 57.
terms.notConfuse: Both numbers are the same for every pair and cannot compare two pairs; use bbox area or utilisation.

terms.meaning: Total block area ÷ bounding-box area. The instructor’s pair gives 23 / 36 = 63.89 % and it changes with the pair.
terms.notConfuse: High utilisation can still overflow the outline; read it together with fit.

terms.meaning: Swap two blocks in one permutation, or in both, to get a new pair. Simulated annealing walks randomly between such neighbours.
terms.notConfuse: One move may leave the packing unchanged, or move many blocks.
